notes: Two home-screen widgets and a Quick Settings tile: a Paste & download button, and a live card that shows what is downloading, what is waiting, and why · Back everything up to one file — the queue, settings and saved sites — and bring it back on any phone: Settings › Rabbit › Backup · Share anything at Rabbit: several links in one message, a text file of links, an IPTV playlist, or a .torrent file — every link found, each queued once · Subscribe to a playlist or channel from the Add page — new videos queue themselves, checked daily · Watch an RSS feed with a pattern like "grand blue*1080" — matching releases queue themselves · Read a magnet out of a picture: the + menu decodes a QR code from a photo or screenshot, entirely on the phone · Recent activity: a searchable timeline of what started, finished and failed — with the reason · The browser grows a Reader mode, counts its find-in-page matches, brings its tabs back after a restart, and downloads just the audio from a held link · Subscribed ad-block lists: paste a hosts or EasyList URL and its domains join the built-in blocker, refreshed daily · Diagnostics shows each torrent's swarm: peers, how many seed, and what flows each way · A site that wants a login says so, with a Log in button — the browser's cookies do the rest · With the app lock on, notifications stop naming your downloads · Held downloads explain themselves in whatever language the phone speaks — the groundwork for translations · Fixed: the same torrent could download twice when its link was written differently — torrents are known by their identity now · Fixed: opening a .torrent file from a share or a file manager works, and takes the torrent's real name · A recorded crash can become a ready-made GitHub issue from Diagnostics — only ever by your hand
